title: Old Testament Stories
intro: Arks, giants, lions and a big fish. How well do you know these famous stories from the Bible?

questions.prompt: In Genesis, on which day did God rest after creating the world?
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:2 says that by the seventh day God had finished his work, and on that day he rested.

questions.prompt: Who built an ark to save his family and the animals from the flood?
questions.explanation: In Genesis 6, God tells Noah to build an ark of cypress wood.

questions.prompt: Who was swallowed by a huge fish?
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:17 says that a huge fish swallowed Jonah, and he was inside it for three days and three nights.

questions.prompt: Which giant did the young shepherd David defeat?
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 17, David defeats the Philistine champion Goliath with a sling and a stone.

questions.prompt: Who led the Israelites out of Egypt?
questions.explanation: In Exodus, Moses leads the Israelites out of Egypt, and God parts the Red Sea for them.

questions.prompt: Who was thrown into a den of lions but kept safe?
questions.explanation: In Daniel 6, Daniel is thrown into the lions' den, and God sends an angel to shut the lions' mouths.

questions.prompt: Jacob gave his son Joseph a special, ornate robe.
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:3 tells how Jacob, also called Israel, made an ornate robe for Joseph.

questions.prompt: How many commandments did God write on the stone tablets given to Moses?
questions.explanation: Exodus 34:28 calls them the Ten Commandments.

questions.prompt: In the story of Noah, for how many days and nights did it rain?
questions.explanation: Genesis 7:12 says rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights.

questions.prompt: In the story of Noah, a dove returned carrying an olive leaf.
questions.explanation: Genesis 8:11 says the dove came back with a freshly plucked olive leaf, showing the water was going down.

questions.prompt: In Genesis, what was the name of the first woman?
questions.explanation: Genesis says Adam named his wife Eve, which sounds like the Hebrew word for living.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the garden where God placed Adam and Eve?
questions.explanation: Genesis says God planted a garden in Eden, full of trees that were good for food.

questions.prompt: In Genesis, God made people on the first day of creation.
questions.explanation: People were made on the sixth day. The first day was when God made light.

questions.prompt: After the flood, what did God put in the clouds as a sign of his promise?

options.label: A cloud shaped like a dove

questions.explanation: God promised never again to flood the whole earth, and the rainbow was the sign of that promise.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the son born to Abraham and Sarah when they were very old?
questions.explanation: Sarah laughed with joy when Isaac was born, and his name means "he laughs".

questions.prompt: Abraham's wife was called Sarah.
questions.explanation: God gave her the name Sarah and promised that she would have a son.

questions.prompt: What was the name of Jacob's twin brother?
questions.explanation: Esau was born first and Jacob was born holding on to his brother's heel.

questions.prompt: How many sons did Jacob have?
questions.explanation: Jacob had twelve sons, and their families became the twelve tribes of Israel.

questions.prompt: Joseph later became a powerful ruler in which country?
questions.explanation: Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of the whole land of Egypt after Joseph explained his dreams.

questions.prompt: When baby Moses was hidden in a basket, where was it placed?

options.label: Among the reeds by the Nile
In a cave in the hills
On the roof of a house

questions.explanation: His mother put the basket among the reeds along the Nile, where Pharaoh's daughter found him.

questions.prompt: Moses had a brother called Aaron.
questions.explanation: God sent Aaron to help Moses speak to Pharaoh.

questions.prompt: What did Moses see on fire that did not burn up?
questions.explanation: God spoke to Moses from the burning bush and sent him to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.

questions.prompt: What was the special food God gave the Israelites in the desert, which they gathered each morning?
questions.explanation: Manna appeared on the ground each morning. Exodus says it was white and tasted like wafers made with honey.

questions.prompt: The walls of which city fell down after the people shouted and the trumpets sounded?
questions.explanation: Joshua led the people around Jericho, and when the trumpets sounded and they shouted, the walls fell.

questions.prompt: Who was very strong as long as his hair was not cut?
questions.explanation: Samson told Delilah that his strength would leave him if his head was shaved.

questions.prompt: Ruth promised to stay with her mother-in-law. What was her mother-in-law's name?
questions.explanation: Ruth said to Naomi, "Where you go I will go", and went with her to Bethlehem.

questions.prompt: Which instrument did young David play to comfort King Saul?
questions.explanation: A lyre is a small stringed instrument a bit like a harp. David's music helped Saul feel better.

questions.prompt: Which king asked God for wisdom and became famous for being wise?
questions.explanation: God was pleased that Solomon asked for wisdom instead of riches, and gave him a wise and understanding heart.

questions.prompt: Which brave queen went to the king to save her people?
questions.explanation: Esther risked going to the king without being called, and asked him to save her people.

questions.prompt: According to Genesis, how many years did Methuselah live?
questions.explanation: Methuselah lived for 969 years, the longest age given for anyone in the Bible.
